# Building the First Eighteen Atoms

<!-- STEP id="h-he" -->
## Hydrogen and Helium

Each element has one more proton and one more electron than the element before it, so we can build the atoms in order. Hydrogen has 1 electron, in K. Helium has 2, and now K is full, because K holds only 2.

<!-- STEP id="li-ne" -->
## Lithium to Neon

Lithium has 3 electrons. K is already full, so the third electron starts the L-shell, and the configuration is 2,1. Each element after that adds one more electron to L, until neon reaches 2,8 and L is full.

<!-- STEP id="na-ar" -->
## Sodium to Argon

Sodium's eleventh electron cannot go into K or L, since both are full, so it starts the M-shell: 2,8,1. M then fills one electron at a time, up to argon at 2,8,8.

<!-- STEP id="takeaway" -->
## A Pattern Repeats

Look at where each row ends and begins. Helium, neon and argon each end a row with a full outer shell, and lithium and sodium each begin a row with one electron alone in a new shell.

**A full outer shell is followed by one electron alone in a new shell, again and again.**

Tap any element and read its configuration. We will soon see why this repeating pattern matters.
